business.title: The first Monday you can take off
business.body: The business can cover a week without you for the first time. Aigerim has a trial customer waiting for a decision, and you have already promised yourself a day away from the studio.
choices: Ask Aigerim to lead the trial
Aigerim ran the trial. On your day off, the first customer message you saw was a report of what she had learned.
Keep the trial small and run it yourself
You ran one short trial and wrote down where the handoff still needed work.

change.title: Someone asks how you got here
change.body: A person from your old industry asks what the switch was like. Daniyar offers to make room at his workshop. Your new team also needs someone to document what made your latest project work.
choices: Tell the whole story at Daniyar’s workshop
You spoke about the rejection as well as the offer. Afterward, someone asked to see the project that opened your first door.
Write a guide for the new team
The team started handing your guide to new colleagues. A shortcut from your old job became the page everyone bookmarked.

grow.title: A decision you can hand over
grow.location: Almaty · The team’s weekly planning room
grow.body: A colleague wants to handle a decision you usually make. Dana asks whether you have enough confidence to let them run it, or whether this is a good moment to show the team how you think.
choices: Give the colleague ownership and stay available
Your colleague made a call you would not have made. You agreed on how to review the result, then left the decision with them.
Make the decision together in the open
You talked through the decision in front of the team. It took longer, but two colleagues used the same method the following week.

abroad.title: The last table by the window
abroad.body: Madina asks what you want to keep from your time abroad. She can connect you with a cross-campus project, or the two of you could protect a regular conversation with no work attached.
choices: Set a monthly call with Madina
You put the call on the calendar. The first month, neither of you had anything impressive to report, which made it easier to keep talking.
Join the cross-campus project
You joined the project. A familiar question returned in a different accent, and you found yourself answering it differently.

local.title: Where the research goes next
local.body: Aliya asks what you want to happen to your work after the presentation. You have time to prepare a version the community can use, or to document a question another researcher could pick up.
choices: Share a practical version with the community
Someone at the presentation showed you how they would adapt your work. You changed the instructions before sending the final version.
Document a question for the next researcher
You left a clean record of the result and one unresolved question. Aliya added it to the lab’s next meeting.

work.title: Show what you learned
work.body: Arman asks you to bring something that shows how you learn. The workshop has room for a public demonstration or a small session on one problem you still cannot solve.
choices: Demonstrate something you shipped
You demonstrated the project and explained where someone else had helped. A new attendee stayed afterward to ask how to get started.
Bring the unsolved problem
You brought the unsolved problem. The best question came from someone who had never worked in your field.

invest.title: A plan for an ordinary weekend
invest.body: Azamat asks what should go on the shared calendar this month. There is a weekend when you could build a small tradition together, or leave the days open and check in when both of you know what you need.
choices: Make a recurring plan together
You chose one recurring breakfast. The first time someone needed to cancel, you rescheduled it together.
Protect one free day each
You each kept a free day. When you met again, you had things to tell each other that had happened separately.

space.title: The next invitation
space.body: A friend’s gathering puts you and Azamat on the same invitation list. You have time to decide how you would like to be there and to let Azamat decide for themself.
choices: Name what contact you’re comfortable with
You sent a short note about what felt comfortable. The gathering was easier once neither of you had to guess.
Make your own plan for the evening
You kept the evening for a plan with Dinara. The invitation stayed unanswered until you were ready to decide.

new.title: A place you choose to return to
new.body: Samat asks whether you want to help with the next reading night. Dinara offers a smaller evening together that would leave more time for the rest of your week.
choices: Help plan the next reading night
You took one task for the reading night. At the next meeting, someone set out a chair for you before you arrived.
Keep the evening small
You shared dinner with Dinara and went home early. The bookstore invitation was still there when you wanted it.
